chunks: 'Abbad al-Basri met Ali ibn al-Husayn (blessings of God be upon him) on the road to Mecca and said to him: 'O Ali ibn al-Husayn! You have abandoned jihad and its hardship and turned toward the Hajj and its ease. Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, says:'

"Indeed God has purchased from the believers their souls and their wealth in exchange for Paradise; they fight in the way of God, so they kill and are killed — a promise binding upon Him in truth, in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran. And who is more fulfilling of his covenant than God? So rejoice in the transaction you have made with Him, and that is the great triumph." [9:111]
So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Complete the verse.' And he said:

"The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, the fasters, those who bow, those who prostrate, those who enjoin good and forbid evil, and those who preserve the limits of God — and give glad tidings to the believers." [9:112]
Then Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'When we find those who possess these characteristics, then jihad alongside them is superior to the Hajj.'

key_terms.الجهاد: Jihad — in this context referring to armed fighting in defense of the faith, not inner spiritual struggle
key_terms.الحج: Hajj — the pilgrimage to Mecca, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.الفوز العظيم: al-Fawz al-'Azim — the great triumph, referring to Paradise as the ultimate success
key_terms.سبيل الله: Sabil Allah — the way/path of God, the righteous cause for which fighting is permitted
key_terms.صفة: Sifa — characteristic, quality; the moral and spiritual attributes that qualify one for jihad

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the conditions for jihad being superior to Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narrative, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, AS) responds to the challenge of 'Abbad al-Basri, a Basran ascetic who questioned why the Imam was performing Hajj instead of engaging in armed jihad. The Imam's response — asking 'Abbad to recite the full verse — reveals that the Quranic injunction for fighting jihad is inseparably bound to the spiritual and moral qualifications of the mujahid. The Imam's conclusion establishes a conditional principle: armed jihad alongside those who truly embody the qualities of faith, worship, and enjoining good is indeed superior to Hajj, but such people are exceedingly rare. This hadith reflects the 4th Imam's context of living under Umayyad tyranny where armed jihad would have been misused; it subtly redirects focus from outward military action to inward spiritual rectitude.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abbad Al-Basry met Ali Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> in a street of Makkah, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> neglect the Jihad (due to) its difficulties, and you<sup>asws</sup> come upon the Hajj and its gentleness. Surely Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying

[9:111] Surely Allah has Bought from the Believers their own selves and their wealth for this, that they shall have the Paradise; they are fighting in Allah's Way, so they kill and are killed; a Promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Evangel and the Quran; and who is more loyal to his Covenant than Allah? Rejoice therefore in the pledge which you have made; and that is the mighty achievement’.
So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Complete the Verse’. So he said, ‘

[9:112] The Penitent, the worshippers, the Praisers, the Fasters, the Bowers, the Prostraters, the enjoiners of good and the forbidders of evil, the preservers of the Limits of Allah; and give good news to the Believers’.
So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When we<sup>asws</sup> see them, those with these characteristics, so the Jihad along with them would be superior than the Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Uthman from ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “’Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ‘Abbad al-Basriy met Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, on the way to Makkah and said, ‘O Ali ibn al-Husayn, you have disregarded Jihad because it is difficult but you have inclined toward al-Hajj because of the ease in it.

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, says, “Allah has purchased the souls and property of the believers in exchange for Paradise. They fight for the cause of Allah to destroy His enemies and to sacrifice themselves. This is a true promise which He has revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, and the al-Quran. No one is more true to His promise than Allah. Allow this bargain to be glad news for them.
This is indeed the supreme triumph.’” [9:111] Ali ibn al-Husayn, Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Complete the verse.’

He then recited: ‘(The believers) who repent for their sins, worship Allah, praise Him, travel through the land (for pious purposes), kneel down and prostrate themselves in obedience to Allah, make others do good and prevent them from sins and abide by the laws of Allah, will receive a great reward. Allow this to be glad news for the believer.’
[9:112] Ali ibn al-Husayn, Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘If we see these kinds of people with these qualities then Jihad along side with them is more virtuous than al-Hajj.’”
